newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rise on Wall Street recovery.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rise on Wall Street recovery.

text.p: French stocks staged a partial rebound on Friday after investors were encouraged by higher bond prices and a rise on Wall Street, brokers said.
The bourse also took heart from the appointments to the Bank of France's monetary policy council of two candidates viewed as likely to favour lower interest rates, they said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index, which fell 2.54 percent on Thursday, recovered 25.79 points, or 1.14 percent, to close at 2,282.76.
For the week, it was down 1.05 percent.
The CAC January futures contract rose 32 points to 2,288.
Volume was a relatively light 3.33 billion francs as many players were still on holiday.
"The New Year will really begin on Monday," a portfolio manager said.

The market welcomed the appointments of monetary "doves" Pierre Guillen, former head of the employers' federation CNPF, and Jean-Rene Bernard, former deputy governor at property lender Credit Foncier, to the nine-member monetary policy council.
But its primary focus is on U.S. interest rates, with many investors worried that increases to quell inflationary pressures may end Wall Street's bull run.
The market will be watching closely next week for key U.S. indicators such as durable goods orders on Tuesday, jobless claims and wholesale prices on Thursday.
The biggest gainers on the bourse on Friday were often the previous day's top losers, such as Compagnie Bancaire, which rebounded 5.80 percent to close at 620 francs.

The car sector showed less resilience. PSA Peugeot Citroen shares recouped 1.26 percent, or less than a third of Thursday's loss on 1996 car sales showing a loss in the French industry's market share.
Freezing weather in Europe boosted shares in oil majors Total, up 2.21 percent at 416 francs, and Elf-Aquitaine, up 1.95 percent at 471.50.

Shares in salt company Cie des Salins du Midi, which resumed trading on Friday for the first time since December 23, was the top gainer with a 38 percent rise to 608 francs, close to the 614 franc-per-share offer proposed on Tuesday by Morton International.
